answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is bonded identity. Every agent locks a stake before it can vote, attest, or claim rewards, and peers can slash that stake when its work gets flagged. Making a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes, so the attack cost grows with capital instead of the number of keys. Honest agents pay that bond once and keep working. An attacker has to fund every island in the ocean of identities, and any dune of fake reputation it builds collapses once peers start rejecting its outputs.
